newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bank stocks down on bond market gyrations.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bank stocks down on bond market gyrations.

text.p: U.S. bank stocks, which have enjoyed a powerful run this year, sold off on Thursday amid gyrations in the bond market.

"This falls firmly in the category of profit-taking triggered by the decline earlier in the bond market and the rise in interest rates," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp. Among the banks selling off were Wells Fargo and Co, down 3-1/2 at 264-1/2; NationsBank Corp, down 2-1/2 at 93-5/8; BankAmerica Corp, down 2-5/8 at 94-5/8; and First Chicago NBD Corp, down 2-3/8 at 51-3/8.
Also down were Citicorp, off 2-1/4 at 98-3/4; Chase Manhattan Corp, off two at 86-5/8; First Citizens BancShares Inc, off 2-3/4 at 77-1/2; and BankAmerica Corp, off 2-3/4 at 94-1/2.

"The performance of bank stocks has been nothing short of spectacular this year. Along with the high technologies, they have been the leaders this year," Johnson said. "It does not take much to trigger profit-taking in high flyers."

Michael Mayo, analyst at Lehman Brothers, attributed the decline in bank stocks to profit-taking. "They were a little overbought," he said. "They have well outperformed the market for the year and it's getting close to year-end."
Mayo said he remains positive on bank stocks and believes the outlook is bright for the next year or two. He expects profits for bank companies to be up 10 to 12 percent in 1997.
